absolute_monarchy.head_of_government: Chief Minister / Grand Vizier / Chancellor (appointed by and serving at the pleasure of the monarch)
absolute_monarchy.foreign: Minister / Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs
absolute_monarchy.interior: Minister of the Interior / Royal Household
absolute_monarchy.military_chief: Commander-in-Chief (often the monarch or a royal prince)
absolute_monarchy.notes: Monarch may act as own foreign minister and commander. Ministers removed by royal dismissal; ruler removed only by death, abdication, palace coup, revolution or foreign conquest. Before c.1900 there is usually no standing intelligence chief: model as a court/police function.

constitutional_monarchy_parliamentary.defense: Minister of Defence (Minister of War / of the Navy before c.1945)
constitutional_monarchy_parliamentary.interior: Minister of the Interior / Home Affairs
constitutional_monarchy_parliamentary.military_chief: Chief of the Defence Staff / Chief of the General Staff
constitutional_monarchy_parliamentary.notes: Monarch reigns but does not rule; PM depends on parliamentary majority.

constitutional_monarchy_executive.head_of_government: Minister-President / Chancellor / Prime Minister (answerable to the crown)
constitutional_monarchy_executive.notes: Parliament controls budgets but cannot directly dismiss ministers; removal is by the monarch.

parliamentary_republic.head_of_state: President (largely ceremonial, elected by parliament or people)
parliamentary_republic.intelligence: Director of the National Intelligence Service
parliamentary_republic.military_chief: Chief of the General Staff / Chief of Defence

presidential_republic.foreign: Secretary / Minister of Foreign Affairs (Foreign Relations)
presidential_republic.military_chief: Chief of the Armed Forces Joint Staff
presidential_republic.notes: Fixed terms; legislature cannot dismiss president except by impeachment.

semi_presidential_republic.head_of_government: Prime Minister (appointed by the president, responsible to parliament)
semi_presidential_republic.intelligence: Director of the State Security / Intelligence Service
semi_presidential_republic.military_chief: Chief of the General Staff / Chief of Defence Staff
semi_presidential_republic.notes: President removed by election/impeachment; PM by no-confidence or presidential dismissal.

one_party_communist_state.head_of_state: Chairman of the Presidium / President of the State
one_party_communist_state.head_of_government: Premier / Chairman of the Council of Ministers
one_party_communist_state.paramount_leader: General Secretary (First Secretary) of the Central Committee
one_party_communist_state.interior: Minister of the Interior / Public Security
one_party_communist_state.notes: Real power sits with the party General Secretary and Politburo; the game should treat the GS as the player's office and state posts as advisors. No-confidence does not exist; removal is by Politburo/Central Committee vote, death, or revolution.

one_party_state.head_of_government: Prime Minister / Leader of the ruling party
one_party_state.intelligence: Chief of the Secret Police / State Security
one_party_state.notes: Legislature is a rubber stamp; removal by coup, party intrigue, revolution or defeat in war.

military_junta.head_of_state: Chairman of the Junta / President of the Revolutionary Command Council
military_junta.head_of_government: Chairman of the Junta (or appointed Prime Minister)
military_junta.foreign: Minister of Foreign Affairs (often a civilian technocrat)
military_junta.finance: Minister of Finance (often a civilian technocrat)
military_junta.interior: Minister of the Interior (usually a general)
military_junta.intelligence: Director of Military Intelligence / State Security
military_junta.military_chief: Commanders of the Army, Navy and Air Force (collectively the junta)
military_junta.notes: No elections or no-confidence; leader removed by counter-coup within the junta, popular revolution, or negotiated return to civilian rule.

personalist_dictatorship.intelligence: Head of the Presidential Guard / Secret Police
personalist_dictatorship.notes: Ministers are courtiers removed at will. Ruler removed by death, coup, assassination or revolution.

theocratic_republic.head_of_government: President (elected; government head under the Supreme Leader)
theocratic_republic.military_chief: Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces
theocratic_republic.notes: Supreme Leader removable only by the clerical Assembly of Experts (never used); president by election, parliamentary impeachment or Supreme Leader dismissal.

revolutionary_government.head_of_state: President of the Provisional Government / Chairman of the Revolutionary Council
revolutionary_government.intelligence: Head of the Revolutionary Security Committee
revolutionary_government.notes: Short-lived and unstable; removal by factional purge, coup or counter-revolution.

colonial_or_occupied.head_of_state: Foreign sovereign (represented by a Governor-General / High Commissioner / Military Governor)
colonial_or_occupied.head_of_government: Governor-General / Military Governor (or a collaborating Prime Minister)
colonial_or_occupied.notes: Not playable as a sovereign actor; foreign and defence policy are controlled by the metropole/occupier. Ends by independence, revolution or the occupier's withdrawal.

dominion.foreign: Secretary of State for External Affairs (handled by London before the 1920s-1931)
dominion.defense: Minister of Defence / Militia and Defence
dominion.interior: Minister of the Interior / Home Affairs
dominion.notes: Parliamentary (Westminster) system; foreign policy autonomy grew after the 1926 Balfour Declaration and 1931 Statute of Westminster.

empire_napoleonic.head_of_government: Emperor (no prime minister; ministers report individually)
empire_napoleonic.interior: Minister of the Interior / Minister of Police
empire_napoleonic.military_chief: Major-General (Chief of Staff) of the Grande Armée
empire_napoleonic.notes: Authoritarian empire with plebiscitary legitimacy; ends by military defeat, abdication or revolution.

removal_mechanisms.no_confidence: Lower house / legislature passes a vote of no confidence (or government loses confidence/supply)
removal_mechanisms.constructive_no_confidence: Legislature elects a successor and thereby removes the head of government (e.g. FRG Art. 67, Spain 1978, Israel since 2001)
removal_mechanisms.general_election: Loses a scheduled or snap general election
removal_mechanisms.loss_of_party_leadership: Ruling party replaces its leader, who then resigns as head of government
removal_mechanisms.royal_dismissal: Monarch/emperor dismisses the minister or head of government
removal_mechanisms.impeachment: Formal impeachment / removal trial by legislature or court
removal_mechanisms.party_congress: Removed by party Central Committee / Politburo / congress (one-party states)
removal_mechanisms.assassination: Assassination (event, not a procedure; listed where historically common)
removal_mechanisms.death_in_office: Lifetime office; ends only with death (plus other listed mechanisms)
removal_mechanisms.religious_council: Removal by a clerical body (e.g. Iran's Assembly of Experts)
removal_mechanisms.junta_decision: Removed by the ruling junta / military high command (e.g. Argentina 1976-83, Brazil 1964-85)
removal_mechanisms.family_council: Royal family / dynastic council deposes the ruler (e.g. Saudi Arabia 1964)
